quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: Roche's fenebrutinib is the first BTK inhibitor to receive (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA accepted Roche's New Drug Application under priority review for fenebrutinib, an investigational oral non-covalent BTK inhibitor, in both relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS) and primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS); Roche says it is the first BTK inhibitor to receive FDA filing acceptance in both. The filing rests on three positive Phase III studies: in FENhance 1 and 2 (RMS) fenebrutinib reduced the annualised relapse rate versus teriflunomide by 51.1% (p<0.001) and 58.5% (p<0.00001) over 96 weeks, with consistent positive trends on disability progression (cCDP12); in FENtrepid (PPMS) it met the primary endpoint of non-inferiority versus Ocrevus, numerically reducing the risk of disability progression by 12% (HR 0.88; 95% CI: 0.75, 1.03). Serious adverse event rates were 9% vs 9% (FENhance 1), 11% vs 6% (FENhance 2) and 19% vs 19% (FENtrepid); liver enzyme elevations were more frequent than with Ocrevus in PPMS, and an imbalance in reported fatalities was observed across the three pivotal studies (deaths at different timepoints with various causes). The safety database covers more than 2,700 study participants. Pharma CEO Teresa Graham: if approved, fenebrutinib could be the first high-efficacy oral therapy for both RMS and PPMS.
